The design log template is `design-backlog-template.md` in this folder. Paths here are relative to the design-kernel skill folder; the stages, the book's excerpts, and the methods are listed in this skill's `SKILL.md`. Where an excerpt describes the book's room — whiteboards, sticky notes, dot voting, a team at a table — these conventions say how a solo + AI team does that step, and they apply.

```mermaid flowchart TD A["Opening
conventions 1–5"] -- "PO authorizes Empathize" --> B["Empathize
conventions 6–7"] B -- "PO authorizes Define" --> C["Define
convention 8"] C -- "PO settles how to diverge and authorizes Ideate" --> D["Ideate: diverge
conventions 9–10"] D --> E["Ideate: converge
conventions 11–15"] E -- "PO chooses; separately authorizes Prototype" --> F["Prototype
convention 16"] F -- "PO authorizes Test" --> G["Test
conventions 17–18"] G -- "PO decides" --> H["Ending
convention 19"] G -. "PO authorizes a return" .-> R["Resume the stage that needs work
convention 26"] ```

**The three loops.** Empathize and Define: the Product Owner and the Scrum Master settle the research and definition together; the Scrum Master records it, and the Designer takes over when Ideate is authorized (convention 3). Diverge and converge: the Product Owner first settles how to open up ideas; the AI can do the work, and a person picks the solution. Prototype and Test: the AI can do the work once each stage is authorized. Any stage decision handed to the Scrum Master still has to be within the written handover and recorded (`../scrum-kernel/overview.md`, convention 12).
Conventions 20–27 hold at every step; see Throughout, below. Apply the entry and return rules in convention 26 at each transition.
The conventions under Stages cover only what differs from the book or adds what it leaves out; for everything else, follow the excerpts.
blocks.heading: Stages

rules.name: Design sprint or the five modes
rules.heading: The Boundary
rules.text: 1. **Design sprint or the five modes** — The Product Owner says which one a question gets. When they do not, the default split is: open a design sprint when a prototype must be tested with role cards before anyone dares to act; otherwise use the five modes; convention 3 says how to record them. When a chat turns up something to research, it can count as empathize material; if it calls for a design sprint, wait for the Product Owner’s permission to start Empathize, then still run that stage (`../design-kernel/conventions/design-log.md`, convention 26).

rules.name: The five modes and the design sprint
rules.heading: The Two Together
rules.text: 2. **The five modes and the design sprint** — They share five names and are two different things. The five modes are modes, not stages: no fixed order, you can go back and forth, and they are the plugin's base and shared toolbox. The design sprint's five stages each stand on one mode, and add the book's steps, a Product Owner decision between stages, and a prototype tested with role cards — a heavy research module beside the Sprint. What a user calls "the IDEO five-stage method" is the five modes themselves, not the design sprint. Do not mix them: an IDEO log does not run the design sprint's steps (no map, Lightning Demos, or storyboard), and a design sprint does not open an IDEO log — its own log already has five chapters. If an IDEO log shows that a prototype must be tested with role cards before anyone dares to act, the IDEO log can count as empathize material. Start the design sprint with Empathize only once authorized (convention 1 above).

rules.name: When to open an IDEO log
rules.heading: The IDEO Log
rules.text: 3. **When to open an IDEO log** — Use one or two methods when that is enough; their output goes into the log they serve — a Sprint's Increment notes, the product log's Notes. When the five modes make a run of their own — more than one or two methods, or more than one session — open an IDEO log: `scrum/ideo-<suffix>/IdeoBacklog.md`, five chapters, one per mode, with no Product Owner gate between them (how this differs from a design sprint: convention 2). Each chapter holds what that mode produced, not every step taken. Before a mode, read its file in `IDEO-modes/`; before a method, read the method's file, as this skill's Use Protocol says.

rules.name: Where it lives and how it ends
rules.heading: The IDEO Log
rules.text: 4. **Where it lives and how it ends** — The log, the prototypes, and the working material live in `scrum/ideo-<suffix>/`. It has no commitment of its own: For holds the relative path to the product log or sprint log it serves, where the commitment is kept. Keep `> Now:` on its own header line with the current mode and next step, followed by `> Waiting for PO:` with the number and short question of each pending decision, separated by semicolons, or `None`. Update both with the log change that causes them; this adds no gate between modes. The conclusions flow back to the log that asked for it — the product log or the sprint log — and the Product Owner decides what changes. When the work is done, keep the log: the first Sprint Review after that archives it (`../sprint-kernel/conventions/sprint-log.md`, convention 17). A prototype whose conclusions will be built goes to the Sprint that builds them, as that Sprint’s specification. If that Sprint is not open yet, keep the prototype in the IDEO folder until handoff. Any other standalone IDEO prototype is deleted when the work is done.
